title: Rework aggregate watermarking + backfill coordinator to eliminate per-model shadow spikes
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem summary: Console per-model usage charts show short-lived 'shadow' spikes and drops after delayed ingestion/backfills. Root cause investigation indicates out-of-order backfill writes + rolling-aggregation windows produce transient double-counts and missing rows for affected model buckets. These artifacts are particularly visible for streaming-prefix and streaming-batch hybrid traffic where the streaming consumer and backfill job both write rollups without a coordinated watermark / idempotency scheme.

Scope: Fix aggregate-generation and backfill wiring so that: 1) late/backfilled events are merged deterministically without producing spikes; 2) rate-limit tallies + quota buckets remain monotonic and reconciled; 3) console charts can display progressive backfill status (pending / reconciled) and not mislead users with temporary overcounts.

Proposed solution: Implement a lightweight backfill-coordinator + event watermarking and idempotent re-aggregation strategy: 
- Introduce a per-shard watermark (ingest_time watermark) used by the rollup job to gate which windows are final vs provisional.
- Backfill job writes to a "provisional_rollup" table with a backfill_batch_id and watermark; routine rollups continue to write "final_rollup" only after watermark advances.
- Merge/compaction job performs idempotent merge of provisional rows into final rows using (model_id, window_start, backfill_batch_id) as deterministic keys.
- Update meter tallies and rate-limit counters to use monotonic delta reconciliation instead of naive add-on-write; counters will store last_applied_offset and ignore duplicates.
- Expose backfill reconciliation state to Console: show provisional overlays (gray hashed pattern) for windows that are written but not yet compacted.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Option A (full reingest + re-aggregate historical data): highest accuracy but long-running and heavy IO for large tenants. Rejected for immediate fix.
- Option B (watermark + idempotent merge): moderate engineering effort, bounded IO, incremental correctness. Chosen.
- Option C (skip provisional writes and accept brief data gaps): minimal changes but poor UX and potential SLA issues. Rejected.

Acceptance criteria: 
- No observed transient >5% overcount spikes in canary models during a synthetic backfill test (see test harness).
- Rate limiter counters show monotonically non-decreasing usage and reconcile to final values within 2 upstream windows after backfill completion.
- Console displays provisional state and a reconciliation timestamp.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema changes: add provisional_rollup table + last_applied_offset columns to counters. (DB migration with zero-downtime write path).
2) Consumer changes: tag streaming writes with ingest_time and shard_watermark. Modify write path to support provisional vs final writes.
3) Backfill coordinator service: lightweight job that sequences backfill_batch_id, publishes watermark, and triggers compaction.
4) Merge/compaction: idempotent SQL + kafka-triggered compaction for small batches, scheduled compaction for large ranges.
5) Console UX: provisional overlays and reconciliation metadata panel.
6) Canary rollout: one small-traffic tenant + model set, synthetic backfill tests, tracer-based verification.

Monitoring & testing:
- Add Prometheus metrics: backfill_batches_inflight, compaction_latency_seconds, duplicate_counter_ignored_total.
- Add Grafana dashboard panels: per-model provisional vs final delta, rate-limit monotonicity check, watermarks per-shard.
- QA harness: backfill-simulator (internal) that injects N-minute delayed events and validates final totals. Test plan PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/12345

Rollout strategy: 
- Stage 1 (dev): run coordinator against dev DB, validate idempotent merges on synthetic data.
- Stage 2 (canary): enable for 2 small customers, watch dashboards for 48h, check billing reconciliation against golden ledger.
- Stage 3 (gradual): enable globally with throttled concurrency and monitoring alerts.

Rollback plan: compaction is idempotent; if regressions occur, pause backfill coordinator and allow existing final_rollup tables to remain (no destructive operations). If counter deltas mismatch, snapshot pre-change state and revert consumer tagging with a short fallback window.

2026-03-02 - Eng Sync: Decided on watermark + idempotent merge (Option B). PM (Sofia Martinez) approved UX overlay approach. Action: Aisha to own prototype compaction job.
2026-03-05 - PR #12345 opened: initial schema + compaction SQL. Requesting review from @devops and @datateam. Noted potential hotspot on shard 7 for large tenants.

2026-03-09 - Code review: @michael.chen requested explicit test for rate-limit monotonicity. Added unit test harness for counters. @rachael.tan asked to document eventual consistency window in Console tooltip.

2026-03-12 - Staging canary: ran 6 hour simulated backfill against a canary tenant (tenant-c1). Observed provisional overlay clear within 12 minutes of compaction. Duplicate counter ignored total = 0 after offset logic fixed.
2026-03-14 - QA: Added Grafana alert rule 'backfill_reconcile_latency > 1800 unless in maintenance'. Marking ticket In Progress while we prepare canary rollout on prod-small.
